summary: Eritrea is one of the world's most closed destinations: virtually every nationality must obtain a visa in advance from an Eritrean embassy, approval can take weeks and is not guaranteed, and separate travel permits are required to leave Asmara.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign cash or travellers' cheques worth USD 10,000 or more must be declared on arrival; keep the certificate you are given to show when you leave. On departure you must be able to show that any foreign currency you spent was exchanged at Himbol, the state exchange, or spent at an official hotel, and you may not take more than 1,000 nakfa out of Eritrea.

source.name: UK FCDO — Eritrea travel advice, entry requirements

notes: Exchange foreign currency only at Himbol (the state exchange) or spend it at official hotels: the UK FCDO says you must be able to account for foreign currency spent when you leave or risk prosecution and a severe fine, and you may not take more than 1,000 nakfa out of Eritrea.
The UK FCDO says you must declare all laptops, mobile phones, cameras and other electronic items on arrival, or they can be confiscated when you leave.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says Eritrea has a cash-based economy and that credit cards are not accepted for everyday transactions. Paying in foreign currency is illegal except at official hotels, which expect euros or US dollars; exchange money only at Himbol (the state exchange), main banks or major hotels in Asmara.

safety.text: Asmara is a relatively safe city, though there is a risk of street crime, especially at night. The UK advises against all travel within 25 km of Eritrea's land borders, where there are landmines; foreign nationals need a permit to travel outside the Asmara region, and consular assistance is severely limited.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says foreign nationals must apply in advance for a permit to travel outside Asmara’s surrounding province, Zoba Maekel, and to some sites in the capital such as the tank graveyard. Tourists apply to the Ministry of Tourism; processing can take several days, permits are not always granted, and they are checked at checkpoints outside Asmara.
The UK FCDO advises against all travel within 25 km of Eritrea’s borders with Djibouti, Ethiopia and Sudan, and warns of landmines near the borders, particularly with Ethiopia and Djibouti.

Bring cash. The Government of Canada says credit cards are not accepted for everyday transactions; declare foreign currency on arrival, exchange it only through Himbol, main banks or major hotels, and keep the receipts, which the UK FCDO says you must be able to show when you leave.

Expect to be largely offline. The UK FCDO says internet access is highly restricted and mostly limited to hotels and a few internet cafes, there is no 3G, international SIM cards do not work, and a local SIM requires a residence permit.

Photographing government buildings and military installations is illegal (UK FCDO), and the Government of Canada also lists airports, ports and uniformed service members. Always ask before taking photos where security personnel are present.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Eritrea?
faq.answer: Yes — virtually every nationality needs a visa arranged in advance through an Eritrean embassy; there is no eVisa or visa on arrival. Apply well before your trip: the Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says a visa is issued ten working days after it receives the application and fee, and approval is not guaranteed.

faq.question: How long does an Eritrean visa take?
faq.answer: The Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says a visa is issued ten working days after it receives the application and fee, and is valid for three months from issue. Approval is not guaranteed, and business visas must first be initiated by your host in Eritrea through the Department of Immigration, so apply well ahead. Confirm requirements with the embassy handling your application.

faq.question: Can I travel outside Asmara in Eritrea?
faq.answer: Only with a travel permit. The UK FCDO says foreign nationals need a permit, applied for in advance, to travel outside Asmara’s surrounding province (Zoba Maekel) and to some sites in the capital. Tourists apply to the Ministry of Tourism; processing can take several days, permits are not always granted, and they are checked at checkpoints.

faq.question: Can I use cards or ATMs in Eritrea?
faq.answer: No for everyday purchases: the Government of Canada says credit cards are not accepted for everyday transactions and Eritrea runs on cash. Declare foreign currency on arrival, exchange it only at Himbol, main banks or major hotels, and keep the receipts — the UK FCDO says you must account for foreign currency spent when you leave.

faq.question: Is Eritrea safe to visit?
faq.answer: Asmara is a relatively safe city, though there is a risk of street crime at night, but the wider picture demands caution: the UK advises against all travel within 25 km of the land borders, where there are landmines, movement outside the Asmara region needs a permit, international SIM cards do not work, and consular help is severely limited. Travel with a reputable operator and follow the rules precisely.
